paper_title: Enhanced Charge Separation in Ternary Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells by Fullerenes

knowledge_points.content: The ternary bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) organic solar cell based on PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM (1:1.05:0.45) achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.42%, a short-circuit current (JSC) of 27.29 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 70%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The OSC fabricated using the ternary composite exhibits device parameters (PCE, FF, Jsc and Voc of 13.42%, 70%, 27.29 mA/cm2 and 0.70 V, respectively)

knowledge_points.content: The binary bulk-heterojunction solar cell based on PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC (1:1.5) demonstrates a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.48% and a short-circuit current (JSC) of 23.05 mA/cm².
knowledge_points.evidence: better than those of the binary BHJ cell (PCE, FF, Jsc and Voc of 10.48%, 65%, 23.05 mA/cm2 and 0.68 V, respectively)

knowledge_points.content: The exciton separation yield of the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC increases from 68% in the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC blend to 94% in the ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: revealed that the ternary composite exhibited faster hole transfer from COi8DFIC to PTB7-Th... which led to an improved exciton separation yield in COi8DFIC (94% compared to 68% in the binary composite).

knowledge_points.content: The addition of PC71BM to the PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC system enables an electron transfer cascade (PTB7-Th → COi8DFIC → PC71BM), which reduces carrier residence time at the interfaces and deactivates back-electron transfer.
knowledge_points.evidence: The COi8DFIC-to-PC71BM electron transfer promoted an electron transport cascade over PTB7-Th, COi8DFIC and PC71BM, which efficiently deactivated back-electron transfer (carrier recombination loss) from COi8DFIC to PTB7-Th

knowledge_points.content: Hole transfer from the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC to the polymer donor PTB7-Th is accelerated in the ternary blend (8 ps) compared to the binary blend (21 ps).
knowledge_points.evidence: the ternary composite exhibited faster hole transfer from COi8DFIC to PTB7-Th (8 ps compared to 21 ps in the binary composite)

knowledge_points.content: Carrier recombination loss occurring at approximately 160 ps is reduced by more than 50% in the ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM composite compared to the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC composite.
knowledge_points.evidence: Additionally, the carrier recombination loss at ~160 ps decreased by >50% in the ternary composite.

knowledge_points.content: The ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM composite exhibits a smoother surface with a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 3.19 nm, whereas the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC composite has a higher RMS roughness of 6.08 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 1e,f indicates that the ternary composite exhibits a smaller root-mean-square roughness (3.19 nm) than that of the binary composite (6.08 nm)

knowledge_points.content: In femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) spectroscopy, the singlet exciton state of PTB7-Th is identified by a short-lived photoinduced absorption (PIA) band at wavelengths greater than 1150 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: The short-lived PIA band at >1150 nm is attributed to the singlet exciton state of PTB7-Th

knowledge_points.content: The singlet exciton state of the non-fullerene acceptor COi8DFIC exhibits a photoinduced absorption (PIA) band centered at 1030 nm with a lifetime of approximately 65 ps.
knowledge_points.evidence: COi8DFIC exhibits a PIA band centered at 1030 nm and decays within 100 ps. This shortlived PIA band likely results from the singlet exciton state of COi8DFIC... COi8DFIC exhibits single-exponential PIA decay with a time constant of 65 ps

knowledge_points.content: Ultrafast electron transfer from PTB7-Th to the acceptors (COi8DFIC or PC71BM) occurs in less than 0.3 ps, as determined by transient absorption anisotropy (TAA) decay measurements.
knowledge_points.evidence: whereas the BHJ films (PTB7-Th:PC71BM, PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC and PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM) consistently show faster anisotropy time decays of <0.3 ps.

knowledge_points.content: The electron mobility in the ternary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC:PC71BM blend ($4.80 \times 10^{-4} cm^2/Vs$) is significantly higher than in the binary PTB7-Th:COi8DFIC blend ($3.89 \times 10^{-5} cm^2/Vs$).
knowledge_points.evidence: The electron mobility in their ternary composite increased by a factor of ~12, that is, from 3.89 x 10^-5 cm^2/(Vs) to 4.80 x 10^-4 cm^2/(Vs)
